ui.meta_description: CreativeLab is an AI product company connecting people and technology, turning ideas into reality. Introducing our products and vision.
ui.og_description: An AI product company connecting people and technology, turning ideas into reality.
ui.hero_lede: Screens with only what you need. Intelligence that runs on your device. We reimagine the things you reach for every day.
ui.ring_viewport: Use the left and right arrow keys to rotate
ui.lineup_sub: Swipe sideways to meet them one by one.
ui.link_appstore: Get it on the App Store
ui.vision_text: We envision a decentralized world that connects people, devices, AI, and the wider world, empowering everyone to freely expand their own universe.
ui.mission_text: We build technology and products that respect human freedom and individual sovereignty over identity, data, and AI, helping more people turn their ideas and potential into reality.
ui.note_kr_store: Available on the Korean App Store.

1.title: Korea Calendar
1.headline: Lunar dates, holidays, solar terms. One screen.
1.pitch: Date calculations finish on your device, so it works in airplane mode too.
1.summary: A Korean calendar that shows lunar dates, public holidays, the sexagenary cycle, and solar terms on one screen. Lunar conversion and holiday rules are calculated on the device with no server, so it works in airplane mode, and the Home Screen widget calculates the lunar date itself. The iPhone widget shows anniversaries coming up within 30 days, and public holidays and substitute holidays appear in red.
1.why: A Korean calendar that puts lunar dates, holidays, the sexagenary cycle, and the 24 solar terms on one screen. A calendar should open even where there is no signal. So we decided date calculations must never depend on a server.

2.title: Song of the Day
2.headline: One song to hear today.
2.pitch: Picks one song a day based on weather, mood, and taste.
2.summary: Music recommendations that pick one song a day from the weather, your mood, and your taste. National popularity charts are assembled directly from public music data, with no server of our own, and a single tap on Listen to the End continues the song in full on YouTube. Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets on iPhone show today's song without opening the app, and tapping opens that song.
2.why: A music recommendation app that picks one song a day from the weather, your mood, and your taste. National popularity charts are assembled directly from public music data, with no server of our own. Since 1.0.14, instead of a 30-second preview, one tap on Listen to the End plays the recommended song in full on YouTube.

3.title: myTV
3.headline: Videos from the web, on your TV.
3.summary: A casting app that sends videos you watch on the web straight to your smart TV. We built each of the three connection methods that different TVs require, and it hands over the original stream rather than mirroring your screen.
3.why: A casting app that sends videos you watch on the web straight to your TV. Because it passes the video address itself to the TV instead of mirroring the screen, playback continues even after you turn off your phone, and quality does not drop.

4.title: Voice Notes
4.headline: Speak, and it writes it down.
4.pitch: Speech recognition runs on your device, so recordings never leave it.
4.summary: A notes app that turns recordings straight into text for meeting minutes. Speech recognition runs entirely on your device, so audio never goes over the network, and it works without internet.
4.why: A notes app that turns recordings straight into text for meeting minutes. Meetings are usually not meant for other eyes, so we run all speech recognition on the device and keep audio off the network. Dictation works even without internet.

5.title: Cardly
5.headline: Snap a business card. It's organized.
5.summary: A business card manager that reads names and contact details from a photo and organizes them. Text recognition runs on the device, and saving to Contacts and exporting to a spreadsheet both work offline.
5.why: A business card manager that reads names and contact details from a photo and organizes them. A business card is someone else's personal information. So we designed this app to make no network requests at all. Backups are exchanged by you as files, not through a server.

6.title: DailyMap
6.headline: A light map for finding what's nearby.
6.pitch: The app reads an open public map directly, with no relay server, to find what's nearby and build running loops.
6.summary: A light map app for finding shops and places near you. The app queries an openly available public map directly, and recommendations are handled on the device in two steps, so there is no relay server at all. In the Running tab, pick a distance and it builds a loop route from where you are, with voice guidance as you run.
6.why: A light map app for finding shops and places near you. The design rule fit in one sentence. With no key, there is nothing to hide. With nothing to hide, no relay server is needed. And with no relay server, the App Store privacy label can read "Data Not Collected."

7.title: AI Mail Reply
7.headline: Drafts your replies for you.
7.summary: A tool that drafts a reply that fits the email you received. It uses two free AI services as backups for each other, and if neither is available, it switches automatically to an on-device draft template.
7.why: A tool that drafts a reply that fits the email you received. A paid model would run at a loss as users grow, so we chose to use only free-tier language models and removed the paid backend.

9.title: Malmoi
9.headline: Korean isn't read the way it's written.
9.pitch: TOPIK vocabulary and pronunciation for learners. Standard pronunciation rules, built as an engine.
9.summary: Vocabulary and pronunciation study for non-native learners preparing for the Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK). It includes 44,391 words from the National Institute of Korean Language's Basic Korean Dictionary, and implements the standard pronunciation rules as a rule engine (94.0% accuracy).
9.why: A study app for non-native learners preparing for the Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK). The name comes from the first Korean-language dictionary, compiled by Ju Si-gyeong. We carried the "no server, no account" structure proven in our Japanese exam app over to learning Korean.

10.title: Kotoba
10.headline: JLPT words, kanji, and listening in one app.
10.summary: Practice JLPT Japanese vocabulary, kanji, and sentence listening in one app. The question bank and audio playback are built into the app, so you can keep studying without an account or an internet connection.
10.why: Practice JLPT Japanese vocabulary, kanji, and sentence listening in one app. We chose exam prep for a clear reason. When review and mock tests run entirely on the device, running costs do not grow as users do.

11.title: Voca Interpreter
11.headline: Face to face, with no internet.
11.summary: A face-to-face interpreter that works where there is no internet. It includes a screen for two people facing each other and situational phrasebooks, and runs translation models on the device, offline.
11.why: A face-to-face interpreter that works where there is no internet. Speech recognition, translation, language identification, and text recognition all run on the device. The network is used only to download language packs, and once downloaded, it interprets even in airplane mode.

12.title: Study in Korea
12.headline: Student life in Korea, on your own.
12.summary: A guide app that helps international students in Korea handle visa and daily-life procedures on their own. The procedure information is built into the app in 6 languages, with no sign-in and no server lookups.
12.why: A guide app that helps international students in Korea handle visa and daily-life procedures on their own. It includes a stay expiry date calculator, a part-time work hours calculator, an 18-item settling-in checklist, a credit converter, and essential contacts, in 6 languages.

13.title: Career Compass
13.headline: Narrow down majors and careers by personality type.
13.summary: Career exploration that narrows down majors and jobs that suit your personality type. Test results are matched on the device and never sent to a server, in 5 languages.
13.why: A career exploration app that uses a personality type test to narrow down suitable majors, jobs, and study methods. Test results are matched on the device and never sent to a server, in 5 languages.

14.title: Fretwise
14.headline: A coach that picks today's chords.
14.pitch: Guitar and ukulele chord fingering and progressions, step by step. The app plays the accompaniment.
14.summary: A practice app for learning guitar and ukulele chord fingering and progressions step by step. A coach built directly on learning theory picks the chords to practice today, and the app plays the songbook accompaniment in time so you can play along. Today's practice, chosen by the coach, appears in Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, and for each song you can find and open a performance video on YouTube. All practice calculations happen on the device.
14.why: A practice app for learning guitar chord fingering and chord progressions step by step. The reasoning was clear. Practice happens offline, and the moment you add a server, personal data collection begins and you give up the "Data Not Collected" label. For a solo developer, a server is a debt to be repaid.

15.title: Singon
15.headline: Your living room becomes a karaoke room.
15.pitch: Use your phone as a microphone, get scored on pitch and timing, and see which key suits you.
15.summary: An app that turns your living room into a karaoke room, with your phone as the microphone. It scores along 4 axes including pitch and timing, and recommends a key. It uses no server and runs entirely within a single page.
15.why: An app that turns your living room into a karaoke room, with one phone as the microphone. Using no server was the design condition for this app. It is complete in a single screen file, and your vocal profile stays only on your phone. Features that need a server, such as sign-in, subscriptions, and social feeds, were left out from the start.

16.title: Sudam
16.headline: A game of Go with AI, no internet needed.
16.pitch: A Go AI engine inside your phone. Play, review, and analyze life and death.
16.summary: AI Go without internet: play, review, life-and-death problems, and life-and-death analysis. An openly available Go AI engine runs inside your phone for offline games and win-rate graph reviews, and for each group of stones on the board it judges life and death, vital points, and move order. When confidence is low, it doesn't force an answer and marks the result as uncertain.
16.why: Go AI usually runs on a server. You have to make an account and connect to the internet to play a single game. We put an openly available Go AI engine entirely inside the phone, so games, reviews, and even life-and-death problems work with no account and no connection.

17.title: Chess Coach
17.headline: Play and learn chess, no opponent needed.
17.pitch: A chess engine and puzzles, built right into the app.
17.summary: A chess game and puzzle app for playing and learning without an opponent. With a chess engine and 1,000 puzzles built in, it makes zero server calls. Available in 5 languages.
17.why: A chess app for playing and learning without an opponent. We removed online matches and all server code, so it makes zero network requests and is complete in a single screen file.

18.title: AI Janggi
18.headline: Janggi, with the official rules.
18.pitch: Setup variants, passing, and point scoring included.
18.summary: An app for playing traditional Korean Janggi with the official rules, including 4 setup variants, passing, and point scoring. The new engine genuinely reads deeper at higher difficulty levels, and the game screen shows the depth the AI just calculated. The rules are implemented in two independent versions whose results are compared automatically.
18.why: An app for playing traditional Korean Janggi with the official rules. It has 4 setup variants, passing, and point scoring, in 5 languages. We stripped out servers, sign-in, and the cloud, so not a single piece of data leaves the device.

19.title: Ttorang
19.headline: Brain training to wake up memory and focus.
19.summary: A collection of brain training games for older adults that wakes up memory and focus. Redesigned with large text and simple controls, with records kept only on the device. Available in 5 languages.
19.why: A collection of brain training games for older adults that wakes up memory and focus. Redesigned with large text and simple controls, with records kept only on the device. No account and no server.

20.title: Q-City
20.headline: A whole city at your fingertips.
20.pitch: A city-building simulation where you zone land and balance power, water, traffic, and budget.
20.summary: A city-building simulation where you zone land and balance power, water, traffic, and budget. Rotate the map in four directions to see behind buildings, and jump straight to a fire. The simulation logic is maintained in three separate versions, and save files are verified to match character for character. In 5 languages.
20.why: A city-building simulation where you zone land and balance power, water, traffic, and budget. No server, no account, no leaderboard. One city, complete on your device.

21.title: Lotto Lab
21.headline: Number statistics from past winning data.
21.summary: A lottery helper that analyzes past winning data statistically to generate and manage your numbers. The winning data is built into the app, so analysis runs without internet.
21.why: A helper that analyzes past winning data statistically to generate and manage your numbers. Honesty was the starting point of the design. Lotto draws are independent and random, so AI cannot raise the odds. So we chose to create value only through easy input, interpretation, and honest wording, not predictive performance.

31.title: BP Diary
31.headline: One line to take to the clinic.
31.pitch: Turns the week of home readings before your visit into the average your doctor looks at.
31.summary: A logbook that guides you to measure home blood pressure morning and evening for 7 days before a visit, and turns it into the one-line average your doctor looks at. See the 7-, 30-, and 90-day averages and trends on a single clinic screen, with records kept only on the device.
31.why: A logbook that guides you to measure home blood pressure properly for the 7 days before a visit. When we gathered reviews of existing blood pressure apps, the complaints clustered in a few places. I thought it would remind me when to measure. I was charged without realizing it. My records disappeared. The text is too small. We chose just one to solve: the 7-day pre-visit course.

34.title: Retro Arcade
34.headline: An arcade we made ourselves.
34.pitch: A collection of original arcade games. No ads, no purchases, no account.
34.summary: An arcade of 27 original arcade games we made ourselves (1.1.0). We use no one else's game files, and every game is our own, with no ads, no purchases, and no account. Available in 175 regions.
34.why: It began as an app that imitated old game consoles, but it relied on other people's game files, so we changed direction. We built every game ourselves and rebuilt it as an arcade collection that runs the same way on the web with the same engine. It started with 7 games in 1.0 and grew to 27 in 1.1.0.

72.title: Sudam Life & Death
72.headline: Life-and-death problems with exactly one answer.
72.pitch: From beginner to top level, step by step. Missed problems come back to solve again.
72.summary: An app with 318 Go life-and-death problems, each proven to have exactly one answer, in 6 levels from beginner to top level. The 106 problems in levels 1 and 2 are free, and missed problems are collected automatically to solve again. No ads, no sign-up, and no internet needed.
72.why: It started from wanting to solve a few Go life-and-death problems every day. We separated the life-and-death problems from Sudam and made a problem book that works without internet, with no ads, no sign-up, and no daily limit on problems.

32.title: Neighborhood Market
32.headline: No server. Just you and your neighbors.
32.pitch: Connect with neighbors using one invite code to buy, sell, and share.
32.summary: A neighborhood secondhand and sharing app where neighbors exchange invite codes and connect device to device, with no company server. Item listings and one-to-one chats stay only on the devices involved, and it supports reporting, blocking, and 6 languages.
32.why: A marketplace where neighbors trade secondhand items directly, with no server, no account, and no database. Devices connect directly, and the code that creates the connection is copied and shared by users themselves. It supports 6 languages, so international residents can use it too.

33.title: Hanja Levels
33.headline: Level-test Hanja, until your hand remembers.
33.pitch: Assigned characters, mock tests, and writing practice in one app.
33.summary: A study app for Hanja proficiency levels that teaches the 1,000 assigned characters from level 8 to level 4, plus Sino-Korean words, with readings, radicals, and total strokes. Mock tests that match the real exam format, writing practice where you trace and match stroke counts, and spaced-repetition review that asks only what you missed all work on the device.

35.title: Korean History Trainer
35.headline: Learn Korean history by hand, down to the order of events.
35.pitch: Original questions with explanations, a timeline game, and a mistake notebook in one app.
35.summary: A study app for the Korean History Proficiency Test (Basic and Advanced) and Korean history for the civil service Grade 9 exam. Every original question comes with an explanation, and there is a timeline game where you place event cards in chronological order, plus a mistake notebook that fills itself. It works on the device with no sign-up.

36.title: English Test Trainer
36.headline: Listen, write, and try again.
36.pitch: Questions in the real test format, dictation, and vocabulary review.
36.summary: An English test study app that practices TOEIC-style LC and RC with original questions and Korean explanations. Dictation training, a spaced-repetition word list, and an automatically built mistake notebook all work on the device with no sign-up.

41.title: Rival Kingdoms
41.headline: Unify the realm, no gacha.
41.pitch: Domestic affairs, diplomacy, schemes, and battle. A turn-based Three Kingdoms strategy played one month at a time.
41.summary: A turn-based strategy simulation set in the Central Plains at the end of the Han dynasty, where you handle domestic affairs, diplomacy, schemes, and battle one month at a time. Portraits and stats are original, and with no gacha, ads, purchases, or accounts, a full game runs to the end even in airplane mode. In 5 languages.
41.why: When we researched, we found a gap on mobile. A turn-based Three Kingdoms game that runs offline, has no gacha, is lightweight, and supports many languages. With no server, there is no shutdown either.

73.title: Unfold
73.headline: Open your own files, without garbled text.
73.pitch: A viewer for TXT, comics, and PDF. It handles encoding and table of contents on its own.
73.summary: A viewer that opens your own TXT, comic, and PDF files without garbled text. It figures out older encodings such as EUC-KR and Shift_JIS by itself, builds a table of contents by finding titles, and sorts ZIP and CBZ comics in the order 1, 2, 10. With no server, your files and reading position stay only on the device.

74.title: Haru - AI Assistant
74.headline: Hand it off by voice, confirm with a card.
74.pitch: Hand off your schedule, to-dos, and expenses. Nothing changes until you tap.
74.summary: An assistant that handles your schedule, to-dos, expense log, email drafts, and alarms when you ask by voice. With no sign-up, Apple Intelligence on your iPhone does the thinking, and Haru shows what it did on a card first, so nothing is applied until you tap Run. Install Haru PC on your computer to hand off and approve PC tasks from your phone.

8.title: ID Photo Studio
8.headline: One photo is all you need for an ID photo.
8.summary: An ID photo editor that turns one photo into dozens of standard sizes, such as 35×45mm and half-card. It detects the face to crop automatically, swaps the background for a solid color, then checks 11 items such as head height and eye level against the standard.
8.why: An ID photo editor that turns one photo into dozens of standard sizes, such as 35×45mm and half-card. Sizes are handled in millimeters, and pixels are calculated only at export.

75.title: LabelLens
75.headline: The ingredient list, from one photo.
75.pitch: Reads the label on the device and flags the ingredients you avoid in red.
75.summary: An app that explains what each ingredient on a cosmetics label does from a single photo of the back, and tells you whether it contains anything you avoid. It reads the label text on the device rather than a barcode, so new products work too, and 14 groups such as fragrance, ethanol, and parabens are marked in red in the results.
75.why: An app that explains what each ingredient on a cosmetics label does from one photo of the back. It reads the label text instead of relying on a product database, so products missing from a database still work, and the photo is deleted right after recognition.

76.title: Barunsem
76.headline: The answer, in textbook form.
76.pitch: Shows fractions, roots, and π in exact form instead of converting them to decimals.
76.summary: A scientific calculator that shows 1÷3+√8 as 1/3 + 2√2, not 3.16…. It computes fractions, roots, and π in textbook form with the decimal value right below, and includes trigonometric and logarithmic functions, unit conversion, and base calculation. No ads and no sign-up.
76.why: A scientific calculator that gives 1/3 + 2√2 instead of a decimal when you enter 1÷3+√8. It calculates without decimal error, so 0.1+0.2 comes out as exactly 0.3, and the history stays only on the device.

77.title: Rehearse
77.headline: Rehearse out loud before you go.
77.pitch: Talk through everyday situations and see which words came across.
77.summary: A conversation app for role-playing 10 situations in English, Japanese, and Chinese, from ordering at a café to passport control and interviews. You speak with a partner and see in color how clearly each word came across, and sentences you stumbled on return as review cards. Speech recognition runs on the device and no recordings are saved.
77.why: A conversation app built on the idea that if you worry about freezing up abroad, you should rehearse before you go. It turns real situations into scripts you speak through with a partner, with no account and everything on the device.

78.title: Invention Note
78.headline: Answer questions, get a patent draft.
78.pitch: From drafting claims to comparing prior art and calculating filing deadlines, on the device.
78.summary: An app that turns your invention idea into a patent specification draft with claims as you answer questions. It checks claim wording, compares your elements against prior art, and calculates filing deadlines such as grace period, priority, and examination request. There is no server, and your ideas are stored only on this device.
78.why: An app that organizes an invention into a patent specification draft. So that ideas not yet filed do not leak, it has no sign-up and no server.

79.title: PlainScan
79.headline: A scanner you search by the words inside.
79.pitch: Reads scanned text on the device, so a single word finds the paper.
79.summary: A scanner that turns contracts and receipts into clean PDFs and reads the text on the device. Type a word like “lease” and it finds that paper, suggests a title from the first line, and shares as PDF or JPG. No watermarks, no sign-up, and no server.
79.why: People often scan contracts and receipts and then cannot find them later. So we made the text readable on the device, so you can find a paper by a word inside it.

80.title: Pill Time
80.headline: Never miss a dose time.
80.pitch: Reminds you on time and records the dose right from the notification.
80.summary: A medication reminder app that alerts you at set times and records “taken” right from the notification. It counts down the pills left and warns you before they run out, with weekly and monthly dose reports and a large-text simple mode. No sign-up, and every record stays on the device.
80.why: A medication reminder app made to be the easiest way to remember when to take your medicine. You can record a dose from the notification without opening the app, and a large-text mode makes it easy for older adults too.

81.title: Proof Workshop
81.headline: Don't just read proofs. Build them.
81.pitch: Stack shuffled proof-step cards in order and weed out the trap cards.
81.summary: A study app that teaches math-major proofs by assembling them from step cards. You weed out plausible but wrong trap cards, and grading shows the first step that went off. It covers 8 subjects including calculus, analysis, and linear algebra, and concepts you got wrong come back for review at growing intervals.
81.why: A study app that starts from the idea that merely reading proofs leaves you stuck on exams. The concept cards, examples, and practice problems are all written in-house, and with no account your progress stays only on the device.

82.title: HomePath
82.headline: The housing aid you may qualify for, in one place.
82.pitch: A few questions to pre-check, and post-lease deadlines turned into dates.
82.summary: A housing aid guide that pre-checks Happy Housing, national rental housing, housing benefit, and youth monthly rent support from a few questions, and turns legal deadlines after signing, such as move-in and fixed-date registration, into dates. It shows routes by residence status and reminds you of upcoming dates with home screen and lock screen widgets. No sign-up, and your answers stay on the device.
82.why: A guide that puts the support you can get when finding a home in Korea and the tasks after signing a lease in one place. It serves Korean citizens, young people, and foreign residents in five languages, and your answers are never sent to a server.

83.title: Rensa Lab
83.headline: Learn chains with one problem a day.
83.pitch: When you miss, it points out what actually happened on the board.
83.summary: An app for learning chain-making puzzles with falling blocks through a problem set. When you miss, it points out what happened on the board, such as a group popped too early, a chain that stopped at 3, or where the starting point was. It has 210 problems in 7 units, a new problem of the day, an easy-on-the-eyes paper-tone screen, and a home screen widget.
83.why: An app for learning chain puzzles from a problem set instead of by feel. It shows why you were wrong on the board itself, and the explanations are generated on the device without internet.

84.title: Haruharu
84.headline: Today's most important three.
84.pitch: See your day on a 24-hour dial, with habits and journaling in one app.
84.summary: A self-care app that helps you focus on the three most important things each day. It places sleep, exercise, and work in color on a circular 24-hour dial, and shows habit checks, mood and short journal entries, and weekly and monthly stats in one place. It works without sign-up or internet, and records stay on the device.
84.why: A self-care app built on the idea of picking just the three things you must do today instead of piling up tasks forever. Your records are handled only on your phone, so each new day can start fresh.

85.title: Tidal Kart
85.headline: Race 3D karts as an animal racer.
85.pitch: Pick one of eight animal racers and hit the course. Drift and use items to turn the race around.
85.summary: Race 3D karts as an animal racer. Pick one of eight animal racers and hit the course. Drift and use items to turn the race around.

86.title: AI Development Studio
86.headline: An AI development studio where AI agents carry a one-line idea through design, code, testing and build.
86.pitch: An AI development studio where AI agents carry a one-line idea through design, code, testing and build.
86.summary: An AI development studio where AI agents carry a one-line idea through design, code, testing and build.

ai.name: AI and Infrastructure
ai.lede: Recognition and reasoning happen on the device. Even when the connection drops, thinking doesn't stop, and your words and photos stay with you.

platform.name: Platforms and Services
platform.vision: Solid, even where you can't see.
platform.lede: The foundation that connects people and the work inside organizations. We refine the structure behind the screen to the same standard.

fintech.name: Fintech and Investing
fintech.lede: Market prices and household numbers, in a form anyone can read. Precise calculation, concise explanation.

chain.name: Blockchain and Distributed Systems
chain.lede: A way for records to prove one another. We bring distributed technology into everyday tools.

security.name: Security and Privacy
security.vision: What you don't collect can't leak.
security.lede: A design with no sign-up and no personal data piling up on servers. The best way to protect something is never to hold it in the first place.

quantum.name: Quantum Security
quantum.lede: So that today's secrets stay secret even when quantum computers arrive. We look ahead to the next generation of cryptography.

gameai.name: Game AI
gameai.vision: A thinking opponent, in your pocket.
gameai.lede: Engines for Go, chess, and Janggi read moves inside your phone. A game goes all the way through without calling a server.

language.name: Language and Voice
language.lede: Transcribing, translating, reading aloud. Your voice and sentences never leave the device.

media.name: Media and Music
media.vision: Screen and sound, wherever you want them.
media.lede: From a small screen to a big one, with the living room as your stage. Devices connect to each other with no relay server.

care.name: Healthcare
care.vision: Everyday health, quietly by your side.
care.lede: Measuring, keeping up, and waking you. Records stay on the device, refined with large text and simple controls.

life.name: Daily Life and Media
life.lede: Dates and directions, music and the big screen. Apps that sit closest to your day.

work.name: Work and Productivity
work.lede: Making it lighter to write down, organize, and hand off.

game.name: Games and Brain Training
game.lede: Go and Janggi, chess and the arcade, the realm of the Three Kingdoms and a single city. Boards for thinking deeply and playing lightly.

learn.name: Learning and Exams
learn.lede: Languages and exams, guitar and career paths. Learning that continues anywhere.

health.name: Health and Records
health.lede: Measure, note, and see at a glance. Records stay only on the device.

shop.name: Shopping and Price Comparison
shop.lede: Scattered prices gathered in one place, showing only what fits your conditions.

ai.name: Unified Control Board
ai.title: Every service, on one screen.
ai.body: It reads the video generator, running programs, graphics cards, and security events directly from each service and gathers them in one place. Built without outside tools, so updating a tool can never stop the board.
ai.alt: Unified control board screen with graphics card usage, memory, temperature, and power cards and live graphs

ai.name: GPU Monitor
ai.title: Your hardware's state, every second.
ai.body: It watches the memory, usage, temperature, and power of servers running AI models at one-second intervals, and raises a warning when a danger level is reached. Values go straight to the browser, so graphs move without refreshing.
ai.alt: GPU monitor screen with usage, memory, temperature, and power bars and a time-based graph

platform.name: International Matchmaking
platform.title: Different languages, one conversation.
platform.body: A matchmaking service connecting users in Korea and Japan. Every conversation is translated, and video calls are supported. The web app, chat server, and video call signaling server are split into three so that load on one never drags down the others.
platform.alt: Chat screen of a Korea-Japan matchmaking service, with each message shown alongside its Korean and Japanese translation

platform.name: Mini ERP
platform.title: An organization's day, on one screen.
platform.body: An internal system for permissions, attendance, leave, projects, tasks, and workload. We designed the data structure first and built a separate dashboard for each role.
platform.alt: Mini ERP dashboard showing today's check-in and check-out, my tasks and deadlines, and remaining leave

platform.name: Community Board
platform.title: A place for posts and replies.
platform.body: A community for sharing and discussing AI video production techniques. We built screens with posts, comments, likes, categories, and profiles.
platform.alt: Community board post list with categories, sorting, and post cards

fintech.name: Stock Dashboard
fintech.title: Indicators, calculated by hand.
fintech.body: A single stock's price, earnings, and technical indicators on one screen. Moving averages and trend indicators are calculated directly rather than left to an outside library, so we can explain why a value comes out the way it does.
fintech.alt: Stock dashboard price chart screen (demo data) with period selection and candlestick and volume charts

fintech.name: Quant Trading Lab
fintech.title: Judgment, divided by role.
fintech.body: A research platform where separate agents handle market analysis, strategy, risk management, order execution, and performance analysis. Backtests and paper trading come first, and loss limits are written explicitly into the system.
fintech.alt: Market data screen of the quant trading lab, with a price chart drawn from public quotes

chain.name: Mining Control
chain.title: Watching and stopping, on one screen.
chain.body: Turn graphics card miners on and off, and see hash rate, temperature, and pool status on one screen. The server controls the mining program directly and stops it on its own when temperature passes the limit.
chain.alt: Mining control screen with hash rate, temperature, and power cards and live hash rate and temperature graphs

chain.name: CoinPilot
chain.title: Rules go through paper trading first.
chain.body: A tool that lets preset trading rules move to real trading only after they have been verified with virtual funds. Stop-loss, investment limits, and the emergency stop are enforced by the engine, and after a restart it picks up exactly where it left off.
chain.alt: CoinPilot screen with backtest conditions, virtual-fund paper trading, the confirmation step before live trading, and the emergency stop

security.name: Whispr
security.title: Conversations don't stay on a server.
security.body: A messenger that connects devices directly and encrypts end to end. The server only brokers the connection and never stores message content, and tests check that directly.
security.alt: Whispr chat screen with a direct peer-to-peer connection, an end-to-end encryption notice, and exchanged messages

security.name: Distributed Storage Vault
security.title: The key lives only in the link.
security.body: Files are encrypted in the browser first, then uploaded to a distributed storage network. The key to unlock them sits in the part of the share link that is never sent to a server, so the storage side cannot see the contents.
security.alt: File list of the distributed storage vault, with an encryption mark and integrity check result for each file

security.name: Login Anomaly Detection
security.title: Spot unusual access first.
security.body: It watches the login records of the authentication server and scores each one with both hand-built rules and the judgment of an anomaly detection model. When risk is high, the account is locked automatically, and results go straight to the dashboard.
security.alt: Login anomaly detection dashboard with successful and failed logins, alert counts, hourly distribution, and live events

quantum.name: Post-Quantum Signature Monitor
quantum.title: Which accounts still use old cryptography.
quantum.body: It records which signature method was used for each login, and marks methods built to withstand quantum computers separately. Accounts still on the old method are visible at a glance.
quantum.alt: Login events table where post-quantum signatures such as DILITHIUM and FALCON are shown in purple in the token algorithm column

quantum.name: Hybrid Key Exchange
quantum.title: Even if one of the two breaks.
quantum.body: It uses today's key exchange method (X25519) together with a post-quantum method (ML-KEM-768), so the session key stays safe even if one is broken. Signatures likewise combine Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65.
quantum.alt: Hybrid key exchange demo output showing key sizes, signature verification, man-in-the-middle blocking, and the result of an attack that assumes X25519 is broken

gameai.name: Sudam
gameai.title: A game of Go with AI, no internet needed.
gameai.body: An openly available Go AI engine runs inside your phone for offline games, and you can review move by move with a win-rate graph.
gameai.alt: Sudam game screen with a Go board and AI analysis markers

gameai.name: Chess Coach
gameai.title: Play and learn chess, no opponent needed.
gameai.body: A chess engine and puzzle problems are built into the app, so both games and puzzles run without calling a server.

gameai.name: AI Janggi
gameai.title: The official rules, as they are.
gameai.body: Play with the official rules, including setup variants, passing, and point scoring. The rules are implemented in two independent versions and their results compared automatically, so a rules error can't slip through unnoticed.

language.name: Voice Notes
language.title: Speak, and it writes it down.
language.body: Recordings turn straight into text and are organized as meeting minutes. Speech recognition runs entirely on the device, so audio never goes over the network.

language.name: Voca Interpreter
language.title: Face to face, no internet.
language.body: Translation models run on the device to interpret offline. It includes a screen for two people facing each other and situational phrasebooks.

language.name: Malmoi
language.title: Korean isn't read the way it's written.
language.body: The standard pronunciation rules are built as a rule engine, pointing out how the letters actually sound. The vocabulary of the National Institute of Korean Language's basic dictionary is built into the app.
language.alt: Malmoi vocabulary and pronunciation study screen

media.name: myTV
media.title: Videos from the web, on your TV.
media.body: We built each of the three connection methods that different TVs require, and it hands over the original stream rather than mirroring your screen.

media.name: Singon
media.title: Your living room becomes a karaoke room.
media.body: Use your phone as the microphone, get scored along four axes including pitch and timing, and see which key suits you. It runs complete in a single page with no server.
media.alt: Singon song search and list screen

media.name: Song of the Day
media.title: One song to hear today.
media.body: Picks one song a day from the weather, your mood, and your taste. National popularity charts are assembled directly from public music data, with no server of our own.
media.alt: Song of the Day recommendation screen

care.name: BP Diary
care.title: One line to take to the clinic.
care.body: It guides you to measure home blood pressure morning and evening for 7 days before a visit, and turns it into the one-line average your doctor looks at. Records stay only on the device.

care.name: Medication Time
care.title: Log it right from the notification.
care.body: It reminds you when to take your medication, and a button on the notification logs whether you took it without opening the app. Notifications and button actions are handled through a queue.
care.alt: Medication Time home screen with the next dose time and today's medication list

care.name: Ttorang
care.title: Memory and focus, every day.
care.body: A collection of brain training games for older adults. Redesigned with large text and simple controls, with records kept only on the device.
